description: Table 1 is a single rendered data table (no plot, micrograph, colour bar or scale bar) listing the measured chemical compositions of four near-rapidly-solidified steel strips in wt.%. It has six column headers — Strips, Fe, Mn, Al, C, Cr — and four data rows. Row 0Cr: Fe Bal., Mn 26.6, Al 9.1, C 1.2, Cr "–" (dash, i.e. no Cr added). Row 3Cr: Fe Bal., Mn 27.6, Al 8.4, C 1.3, Cr 2.8. Row 6Cr: Fe Bal., Mn 29.1, Al 9.9, C 1.2, Cr 6.8. Row 9Cr: Fe Bal., Mn 27.7, Al 9.5, C 1.3, Cr 9.3. Across the series Mn spans 26.6–29.1, Al 8.4–9.9, C 1.2–1.3, while only Cr varies systematically, rising monotonically to 9.3 wt.%. The table is the composition record that defines the Fe–28Mn–9Al–1.2C-xCr (x = 0, 3, 6, 9) strip series; every other figure in the paper (microstructure, carbide formation, engineering stress–strain curves of as-cast and annealed strips) is indexed by these four strip labels, and the measured Cr contents (2.8, 6.8, 9.3) are close to the nominal 3, 6 and 9 wt.% targets.

subfigures.description: A single rendered table, header row 'Strips, Fe, Mn, Al, C, Cr' and four data rows for the strips 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr; all Fe entries read 'Bal.', Cr entries are '–', 2.8, 6.8 and 9.3, Mn 26.6/27.6/29.1/27.7, Al 9.1/8.4/9.9/9.5, C 1.2/1.3/1.2/1.3.

observations.observation: The table has six column headers printed as 'Strips', 'Fe', 'Mn', 'Al', 'C', 'Cr', with the caption stating the values are in wt.%.
Four sample rows are labelled '0Cr', '3Cr', '6Cr' and '9Cr'.
The Fe entry is 'Bal.' (balance) in all four rows; no numeric Fe value is printed.
The Cr column reads '–' for 0Cr, then 2.8, 6.8 and 9.3 for 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr, i.e. it increases monotonically across the series.
Mn content is printed as 26.6 (0Cr), 27.6 (3Cr), 29.1 (6Cr) and 27.7 (9Cr) wt.%.
Al content is printed as 9.1 (0Cr), 8.4 (3Cr), 9.9 (6Cr) and 9.5 (9Cr) wt.%.
C content is printed as 1.2 for 0Cr, 1.3 for 3Cr, 1.2 for 6Cr and 1.3 for 9Cr wt.%, i.e. essentially constant at 1.2–1.3 wt.%.
The caption states the table gives the measured compositions of the studied steel strips in wt.%.
The citing text states the composition of the studied material is expressed as Fe–28Mn–9Al–1.2C-xCr (x = 0, 3, 6, 9) (wt.%).
The citing text states the actual composition of the strips was detected by Inductively Coupled Plasma mass spectrometry (ICP), so these are measured rather than nominal values.
The measured Cr values (2.8, 6.8, 9.3 wt.%) are slightly below the nominal 3, 6 and 9 wt.% targets of the designed series.
The citing text reports measured average densities of 6.49, 6.45, 6.46 and 6.43 g/cm3 for the 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr strips respectively, but no density column appears in this table.

The citing text refers to Table 1 for 'the detailed value about tensile properties of the annealed strips', which Table 1 does not contain — it lists only chemical composition; this is a caption/citation disagreement reported as both readings.
